title: Assignment 7: Stop Before the Wall with ROS 2
description: Write a complete ROS 2 node in build_node() that drives forward and stops before a wall, using the readings straight ahead in a 270-degree scan.
assignment_html:
Scenario

Purpose: Write a complete ROS 2 node that drives a robot forward and stops it before it reaches a wall. You decide how to read the scan and how to structure the node.

The robot has a laser scanner on /scan and takes velocity commands on /cmd_vel. Unlike Assignment 6, this scan covers the sides as well as the front, so you need the readings that point straight ahead.

File and editing rule

Read the complete project tree, but edit only:

src/wall_stop/wall_stop/controller.py

Write your node inside build_node() and return it. Do not change main(), and do not rename the package, executable, topics, or build_node().

controller.py may import only rclpy, geometry_msgs, sensor_msgs, and math.

New ideas in this assignment

  • build_node() is yours to design. Either define a class that extends Node (add from rclpy.node import Node) and return an instance, or call rclpy.create_node('wall_stop') and attach your publisher and callback to it. Both are accepted.
  • This scan is symmetric. It starts at −135° (right) and ends at +135° (left), so its middle reading, scan.ranges[len(scan.ranges) // 2], points straight ahead. Reading i points at scan.angle_min + i * scan.angle_increment radians.
  • A reading of positive infinity means nothing was detected within range, so the way is clear. This is different from Assignment 6, where the lab treated infinity as unusable. Here the usual ROS convention (REP 117) applies.

Task

  1. Create a Twist publisher on /cmd_vel and subscribe to sensor_msgs/msg/LaserScan on /scan.
  2. When nothing is close in front of the robot, publish a forward speed between 0.1 and 0.3 m/s.
  3. When the wall in front is 0.3 m away or closer, publish linear.x = 0.0. Choose your own stop distance, but do not stop while the wall is more than 1.0 m away.
  4. When the wall moves away again, drive forward again.
  5. Never turn: keep angular.z = 0.0.
  6. Publish at least 5 commands per second. One command per scan is enough, because scans arrive about 12 times per second.
  7. Keep the speed and the stop distance in named constants, such as FORWARD_SPEED and STOP_DISTANCE.

What Run Tests checks

  • Before anything is scored: only allowed imports; build_node() exists and main() is still there; the package builds; the node starts and publishes on /cmd_vel; build_node() returns a ROS node. If one of these fails, the score is 0.
  • Behaviour: the grader publishes synthetic scans of a flat wall straight ahead and watches /cmd_vel. Each situation lasts 1 second (about 12 scans), and the first 0.3 s is not checked so your node has time to react. The situations, in order, are: nothing in range; wall at 1.2 m; wall at 0.3 m; wall at 0.2 m; wall still at 0.2 m; wall back at 1.2 m. Forward means linear.x between 0.1 and 0.3 m/s. Stopped means linear.x within ±0.001 m/s. angular.z must stay within ±0.001 rad/s in every command. Distances between 0.3 m and 1.0 m are not tested. Stopping only earns credit when the robot also drives when the way is clear.
  • Code checks: a Twist publisher on /cmd_vel and a LaserScan subscription on /scan exist while the node runs; the code reads scan.ranges; there is no while True loop or sleep(); main() is unchanged; the speed and the stop distance are named constants; and there are no unused imports that you added.

The grader publishes synthetic scans and observes velocity commands. No robot simulator is used, and it is not a real-robot safety certification.

How scoring works

Behaviour is worth 70% (eight checks), code checks 20% (five checks), and code quality 10% (two checks). The untouched starter earns 0% because build_node() returns nothing. The task counts as passed when everything before scoring passes and all eight behaviour checks pass. Code and quality points add to the score but do not decide passing.

import rclpy
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist
from rclpy.executors import ExternalShutdownException
from sensor_msgs.msg import LaserScan


def build_node():
    """Create your node, connect /scan and /cmd_vel, and return the node.

    Use a class (class WallStop(Node): ...) or plain functions with
    rclpy.create_node('wall_stop'). Both are accepted.
    """
    # Write your code here.
    return None


def main(args=None):  # Do not change main().
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    node = build_node()
    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except (KeyboardInterrupt, ExternalShutdownException):
        pass
    finally:
        node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.try_shutdown()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

Treats positive infinity as unusable or as an obstacle (the Assignment 6 rule), so the robot never moves in open space.
The stop distance is more than 1.0 m, so the robot stops while the wall is still far away.
The comparison drives when the wall is near and stops when the way is clear.
Motion is timed instead of decided from scan.ranges.

solution_html:
Approach

  1. Inside build_node(), create the node, a Twist publisher on /cmd_vel and a LaserScan subscription on /scan, and return the node.
  2. In the scan callback, take a few readings around the middle of scan.ranges (the middle one points straight ahead) and skip NaN.
  3. Publish FORWARD_SPEED when the nearest of those readings is greater than STOP_DISTANCE; positive infinity counts as clear. Otherwise publish zero.
  4. Leave angular.z at 0.0 and publish once per scan, so motion resumes on the first clear scan.
